stemBlocks.value: OPQL is a parallelogram with OP = r and OL = s. T is the point such that vector PQ = vector QT. M divides PL in the ratio 2 : 1. (i) Find, in terms of r and s, a) vector PL and b) vector OM. (ii) Prove that O, M and T are collinear.
Think first: In a parallelogram opposite sides are equal vectors, so PQ is just s — that single fact unlocks both T and M.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p278-q01 from workbook page 278.

solutionSteps.instruction: Travel from P to L through O using the triangle law.
Find PM, remembering M divides PL in the ratio 2 : 1 so PM is two-thirds of PL.
Add OP and PM to reach M from O.
Express OT. Since OPQL is a parallelogram, PQ = OL = s, and QT = PQ = s as well.

contentBlocks.value: OT = OP + PQ + QT = r + s + s
Result: OT = 3 OM, so OT is parallel to OM and they share the point O — hence O, M and T are collinear

strategyBlocks.value: Use PQ = OL = s to place Q and T, build PL by going P → O → L, take two-thirds of PL to reach M from P, then show OT is a scalar multiple of OM.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) a) PL = s − r  b) OM = (1/3)(r + 2s) = (1/3)r + (2/3)s.  (ii) OT = r + 2s = 3 OM; since OT is a scalar multiple of OM and both start at O, the points O, M and T lie on the same straight line.

whyThisWorks.value: A vector route between two points can be built from any chain of known vectors, so P → O → L gives PL without needing coordinates. A ratio along a line converts directly into a fraction of the whole vector, which is why PM = (2/3)PL. Collinearity is proved when one vector equals a number times another and the two vectors share a starting point — parallel plus a common point forces a single straight line.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing PL = r − s by going the wrong way round; PL starts at P, so the r term must be negative.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing PL = r − s by going the wrong way round; PL starts at P, so the r term must be negative.

commonErrors.misconception: Taking PM as (1/2)PL or (2/1)PL instead of (2/3)PL.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Taking PM as (1/2)PL or (2/1)PL instead of (2/3)PL.

commonErrors.misconception: Assuming PQ = r; in parallelogram OPQL the side PQ matches OL, not OP.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Assuming PQ = r; in parallelogram OPQL the side PQ matches OL, not OP.

commonErrors.misconception: Stopping after showing OT and OM are parallel without mentioning the common point O.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Stopping after showing OT and OM are parallel without mentioning the common point O.

examTip.value: For a collinearity proof, always end with the sentence naming the shared point — 'parallel and share point O, therefore collinear' — because that is where the mark sits.
